sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Upland cotton is a robust herb or shrub native to tropical America and widely cultivated. Plants are often 1–2 m tall and may reach about 4 m.

sections.title: Flowers and bolls
sections.text: The leaves are heart-shaped and often divided into three to five lobes. Cream to pale yellow flowers have five petals and sometimes a dark centre. The 2–5 cm boll opens when ripe, releasing seeds surrounded by cotton fibres.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: The seeds contain gossypol and require appropriate processing; do not eat raw seeds.
